summary.text: Yes. Licensees may advertise these programmes when the healthcare service is part of a government-funded, initiated or endorsed programme.

details.heading: What licensees may advertise
details.body: A licensee may advertise government programmes when the advertisement gives factual information about, or related to, the healthcare services they provide. The service must be part of a programme funded, initiated or endorsed by the Government or the Health Promotion Board.

example_phrasings: Can a licensee advertise government programmes such as CHAS schemes, health screenings and vaccinations?
Can healthcare providers advertise government health programmes?
Are licensees allowed to promote CHAS and vaccinations?

sources.page_title: Can a licensee advertise government programmes such as CHAS schemes, health screenings and vaccinations?

quotes.text: Licensees are allowed to advertise government programmes if the substantive content comprises factual information about or relating to the healthcare services provided by a licensee, where the healthcare service is provided in relation to a programme that is funded (in whole or in part), initiated or endorsed by the Government or the Health Promotion Board.
